findings.description: `CommittedDayRecorder.on_day_records` sets `t_sus_ms` with `row.get("t_sus_ms", 0.0)`, so any row whose sample lacks the field, including every batch that is not the final one, is exported as `0`. The benchmark treats this column as a required measurement, so a zero that means 'not measured' is indistinguishable from a real zero reading.
findings.title: Unmeasured t_sus_ms is written as a fake zero

findings.description: `auth_measure_start_us`/`auth_measure_end_us` now come from the worker's `produced_at_us` stamps for the warmup-boundary day and the last measured day. The old code used main-thread `Time.get_ticks_usec()` at the moment each commit was observed. `perf_change_check.py` runs each commit's own copy of this script and keys archived records only by `METHOD_VERSION = 2`, which has not changed. So any `compare` with a base before this PR and a head after it reports a change in the headline metrics `auth.authoritative_days_per_second` and `harness.adjusted_days_per_second` that comes only from the new measurement method.
findings.title: Headline throughput changes meaning across this commit

evidence.explanation: The new code takes both ends of the interval from worker commit timestamps (recorder.warmup_finished_us / last_measured_us, set from record["produced_at_us"]). That leaves out the main-thread consumption latency that the old observation timestamps included. The perf tool runs PERF_SCRIPT from each commit's worktree, treats these two values as HEADLINE metrics, and puts only the fixed METHOD_VERSION in the archive identity. Base and head records from either side of this PR therefore measure different intervals under the same method identity.

findings.description: `CommittedDayRecorder.on_day_records` writes the foreground timing sample and `runtime_graph_*` worker metrics only on a batch’s final row when the snapshot’s committed day and generation match, leaving other rows’ metric cells blank. When publication groups days differently between runs, `csv_metrics` skips those blanks and computes mean, p95, and max over different subsets of days, making base-versus-head summaries reflect batching as well as performance.
findings.title: Per-day CSV timing columns cover only some days

evidence.explanation: The recorder calls `_build_row` with the sample only when `index == records.size() - 1` and the snapshot matches `tick_idx`; other records retain empty metric cells. The adapter can publish multiple day records in one batch, and `csv_metrics` skips blank CSV cells when calculating numeric summaries, so batch grouping determines which rows contribute.

findings.description: `_run` calculates `authoritative_days_per_second` from `run_started` to `last_measurement_received_us` when `warmup_days == 0`, but uses worker `produced_at_us` stamps when warmup is positive. The zero-warmup interval therefore includes calendar setup and main-thread writeback and publication latency, and can fall below the 50 days/s checkpoint even when native commit production meets it.
findings.title: Zero-warmup throughput counts startup time
